40:24.heading: Ayah 24

blocks.text: to Pharaoh, Hāmān and Korah, but they said, “A magician! An utter liar!”

‘to Pharaoh, Hāmān and Korah, but they said, “A magician! An utter liar!”’ brings the leading figures of a whole system of power together in one sentence. Pharaoh stands at the head of political authority; elsewhere, Haman appears as the person who manages and carries out its projects; and Korah possesses wealth and economic influence. Moses’ call confronted more than one individual or social class: it challenged the centers of power on which the whole system rested. Yet their combined response offered no answer to the signs and proof described in “with Our signs and compelling proof”. Their position was reduced to two accusations: “A magician! An utter liar!” This exposes a recurring tactic when an opponent cannot answer the evidence: shift the dispute away from the message and attack the character of its bearer, until a brief accusation takes the place of a reasoned answer.

40:26.heading: Ayah 26

blocks.text: Pharaoh said, “Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord! For I fear that he may change your religion or spread corruption in the land.”

“Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord!” is more than a threat: Pharaoh is seeking the approval of his leading men and the wider public. He wants permission to kill Moses and challenges Moses’ Lord to prevent it. This is a fallacy. Allah’s existence and power do not amount to a promise that believers will never suffer harm in this world. The Quran itself says that a believer may fight and be killed or attain victory (4:74), and condemns the wrongful killing of prophets.

This progression shows that clarity in calling people to Allah may develop with the situation. Each stage needs its appropriate degree of explanation, so that caution does not become concealment that loses the truth, and openness does not become rashness that defeats its purpose.

40:48.heading: Ayah 48

blocks.text: Those who were arrogant will say, “We are all in it. Allah has already passed judgment among [His] slaves.”

The arrogant leaders answer: “We are all in it. Allah has already passed judgment among [His] slaves”. A leader who promised protection and held decision-making power in this world cannot ease anything for his followers in the Hereafter. He admits that he shares their fate. The idea of relying on the powerful collapses completely. The follower thought closeness to the arrogant ruler would secure protection or advantage; the ruler benefited from followers who strengthened his authority. When Allah’s judgment comes, each is revealed to have used the other without possessing any means to save them. The judgment restores everyone to their true position: servants under Allah’s decree.

40:49.heading: Ayah 49

blocks.text: Those who are in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, “Pray to your Lord to lighten for us the punishment for just one day.”

When those in the Fire despair of the arrogant leaders, they turn to the keepers of Hell: “Pray to your Lord to lighten for us the punishment for just one day”. They do not ask for complete release, but for a single day of relief. This shows the weight of their suffering after a time when returning to Allah was possible through deeds easy in comparison with this fate. Those who once mocked Moses’ call to his Lord now ask the angels to pray to their Lord. Supplication was an open door in this world; here, after the period of responsibility and action has ended, the request no longer changes the judgment.

40:50.heading: Ayah 50

blocks.text: They will say, “Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?” They will say, “Yes.” They will say, “Then keep praying! The prayer of the disbelievers is only in vain.”

The keepers respond with a question that takes the issue back to its foundation: “Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?” Those in the Fire answer: “Yes”. The problem, then, was not an absence of evidence: clear proofs had reached them. They are told: “Then keep praying!” The Quran adds: “The prayer of the disbelievers is only in vain”. Their plea brings no result because the opportunity to respond through faith and action has ended. The surah’s contrast reaches its height here: people disputed Allah’s signs while the proofs were before them, then, after seeing the Fire, ask for a door that will not open. What matters is not acknowledging truth once seeing it has become unavoidable, but responding when it comes as evidence inviting the heart to believe.

40:52.heading: Ayah 52

blocks.text: the Day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will be of no benefit to them; and they will be cursed and for them there will be the worst abode.

“the Day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will be of no benefit to them; and they will be cursed and for them there will be the worst abode”. In this world there was time to reason, ask, reconsider, and correct wrongdoing. Once the witnesses stand, excuses no longer provide a means of rescue. This answers the person who prolongs argument in this world to postpone responding: a day will come when even skill at making excuses is useless. Another verse clarifies this meaning: “Here you are, you are those who argue on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will argue on their behalf before Allah on the Day of Resurrection” (4:109). The problem is not that a person cannot formulate an excuse, but that the time for excuses has ended after they chose their path in the face of clear proofs.

40:53.heading: Ayah 53

blocks.text: We gave Moses guidance, and made the Children of Israel inherit the Scripture,

“We gave Moses guidance, and made the Children of Israel inherit the Scripture” follows Pharaoh’s fall and opens a scene beyond oppression: guidance, Scripture, and law. The mention of the Scripture is linked here to the period after Pharaoh’s destruction. Laws that organize a society, including retribution, governance, and the community’s other rulings, require circumstances in which they can be implemented. Inheriting the Scripture therefore marked the Children of Israel’s entry into a new phase after tyranny.

40:54.heading: Ayah 54

blocks.text: as a guide and a reminder to people of understanding.

The Scripture served “as a guide and a reminder to people of understanding”. Gaining power is not an end in itself. If Pharaoh is removed but the community then lives without guidance, it returns to other forms of error. What lasts and builds is revelation that guides, and a reminder that awakens people of understanding so they do not reproduce what they escaped. After scenes filled with disputes over the signs, oppressive rule, and projects that divert people from reality, the Scripture supplies an enduring answer. The aim is not merely to dismantle a present falsehood, but to form minds and hearts that return to Allah’s guidance and retain the reminder.
